### `#076` (`Int-2`) — Luogu P4313 [SHOI2012]: 文理分科 (Arts and Sciences Division)

- **Judge URL**: `https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P4313`
- **Constraints**: $N \times M \le 100 \times 100$ classroom grid ($10^4$ students); individual happiness $A_{r,c}, B_{r,c} \le 500$, 5-cell cross unanimity bonuses $S^{\text{art}}_{r,c}, S^{\text{sci}}_{r,c} \le 500$. Time Limit: 1.0 s.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)

Each student at $(r, c)$ chooses **Arts** ($x_{r,c} = 1$, reward $A_{r,c}$) or **Science** ($x_{r,c} = 0$, reward $B_{r,c}$). Furthermore, each student $(r, c)$ receives an extra bonus $S^{\text{art}}_{r,c}$ if $(r, c)$ **and all of its 4-connected orthogonal neighbors** choose Arts, and $S^{\text{sci}}_{r,c}$ if that entire $\le 5$-cell cross chooses Science. Maximize total happiness.

This is the classic 2D grid realization of `#075`: each cell $(r, c)$ defines a higher-order conjunction over the cross stencil

$$N^+[r, c] = \{(r, c), (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), (r, c+1)\} \cap \text{Grid},$$

of size $3 \le |N^+[r, c]| \le 5$.

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

Let $u = \text{id}(r, c) \in \{1, \dots, NM\}$. The total happiness is:

$$\Psi(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{u=1}^{NM} \left[ A_u x_u + B_u(1 - x_u) + S^{\text{art}}_u \prod_{v \in N^+[u]} x_v + S^{\text{sci}}_u \prod_{v \in N^+[u]} (1 - x_v) \right].$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Graph Compilation)

- **Vertex Allocation ($3NM + 2 \le 30\,002$ vertices)**:
  - Student node $u \in [1, NM]$.
  - Arts cross-hub $y_u = NM + u \in [NM + 1, 2NM]$.
  - Science cross-hub $z_u = 2NM + u \in [2NM + 1, 3NM]$.
- **Arcs ($\le 13NM$ directed arcs)**:
  - Apply Recipe 1 to $(A_u, B_u)$ at each student $u$.
  - If $S^{\text{art}}_u > 0$: add $S^{\text{art}}_u$ to `ans_base`, wire $S \xrightarrow{S^{\text{art}}_u} y_u$, and wire $y_u \xrightarrow{\infty} v$ for all $v \in N^+[u]$ (**including $v = u$ itself!**).
  - If $S^{\text{sci}}_u > 0$: add $S^{\text{sci}}_u$ to `ans_base`, wire $z_u \xrightarrow{S^{\text{sci}}_u} T$, and wire $v \xrightarrow{\infty} z_u$ for all $v \in N^+[u]$ (**including $v = u$ itself!**).

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

> [!WARNING]
> **Failure-Mode Guard (`Luogu P4313`)**: The #1 implementation bug on `文理分科` is looping over the $4$ direction offsets `dr = {-1, 1, 0, 0}, dc = {0, 0, -1, 1}` while **forgetting to include the center cell `(r, c)` (`dr = 0, dc = 0`)** in the stencil $N^+[r, c]$! If you omit $y_u \xrightarrow{\infty} u$, student $u$ can choose Science ($x_u = 0$) while their $4$ neighbors choose Arts ($x_v = 1$) and still falsely collect the Arts unanimity bonus $S^{\text{art}}_u$! Always use a 5-element direction array `dr = {0, -1, 1, 0, 0}`.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints (`#076` — Luogu P4313)"}
- **Hint 1**: Treat each cell $(r, c)$'s 5-cell cross neighborhood $N^+[r, c]$ as a subset in `Luogu P1361`.
- **Hint 2**: Make sure your direction array has $5$ entries `dr = {0, -1, 1, 0, 0}, dc = {0, 0, 0, -1, 1}` so the center student $(r, c)$ is linked to their own hubs $y_{r,c}$ and $z_{r,c}$.
- **Hint 3**: With $30\,002$ vertices and $\sim 1.3 \cdot 10^5$ edges, Dinic with Recipe 1 unary normalization runs in $< 30\text{ ms}$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="C++ Model Compilation (`#076` — Luogu P4313: 文理分科)"}
```cpp
void solve_p4313() {
    int N, M;
    cin >> N >> M;
    int NM = N * M;
    auto id = [&](int r, int c) { return r * M + c + 1; };

    vector<long long> A(NM + 1), B(NM + 1), SA(NM + 1), SB(NM + 1);
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) cin >> A[id(r, c)];
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) cin >> B[id(r, c)];
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) cin >> SA[id(r, c)];
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) cin >> SB[id(r, c)];

    int S = 0, T = 3 * NM + 1;
    Dinic<long long> G(T + 1);
    const long long INF = 1e15;
    long long ans_base = 0;

    for (int u = 1; u <= NM; ++u) {
        ans_base += max(A[u], B[u]);
        if (A[u] > B[u]) G.add_edge(S, u, A[u] - B[u]);
        else if (B[u] > A[u]) G.add_edge(u, T, B[u] - A[u]);
    }

    const int dr[5] = {0, -1, 1, 0, 0};
    const int dc[5] = {0, 0, 0, -1, 1};

    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) {
            int u = id(r, c);
            int y_u = NM + u;
            int z_u = 2 * NM + u;
            if (SA[u] > 0) {
                ans_base += SA[u];
                G.add_edge(S, y_u, SA[u]);
                for (int d = 0; d < 5; ++d) {
                    int nr = r + dr[d], nc = c + dc[d];
                    if (0 <= nr && nr < N && 0 <= nc && nc < M)
                        G.add_edge(y_u, id(nr, nc), INF);
                }
            }
            if (SB[u] > 0) {
                ans_base += SB[u];
                G.add_edge(z_u, T, SB[u]);
                for (int d = 0; d < 5; ++d) {
                    int nr = r + dr[d], nc = c + dc[d];
                    if (0 <= nr && nr < N && 0 <= nc && nc < M)
                        G.add_edge(id(nr, nc), z_u, INF);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    cout << ans_base - G.max_flow(S, T) << "\n";
}
```

### `#077` (`Adv-1`) — Luogu P1646 [国家集训队]: happiness

- **Judge URL**: `https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P1646`
- **Constraints**: $N \times M \le 100 \times 100$ classroom grid; unary happiness $A_{r,c}, B_{r,c} \le 1000$, adjacent-pair same-choice bonuses $E^{\text{art}}_{e}, E^{\text{sci}}_{e} \le 1000$ for all horizontal and vertical grid edges $e = \{u, v\}$. Time Limit: 1.0 s.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)

Unlike `Luogu P4313` (`文理分科`, `#076`), where bonuses are awarded to **5-cell crosses** ($|C| = 5$), in `Luogu P1646` (`happiness`) bonuses are awarded to **2-cell adjacent deskmate pairs** $e = \{u, v\}$ ($|C| = 2$): if both $u$ and $v$ choose Arts ($x_u = x_v = 1$), they gain $E^{\text{art}}_e$; if both choose Science ($x_u = x_v = 0$), they gain $E^{\text{sci}}_e$.

Because $|C| = 2$, every synergy term is **quadratic**! This gives us a direct head-to-head comparison between:

- **Method A (Auxiliary Hub Compilation)**: Creating $2$ hubs per grid edge ($\approx 4NM$ extra vertices and $12NM$ extra directed arcs), vs.
- **Method B (Hu Botao's Symmetric Half-Edge Compilation / `合并点边法`)**: Eliminating **all** auxiliary vertices by absorbing $\frac{1}{2}E^{\text{art}}_e$ and $\frac{1}{2}E^{\text{sci}}_e$ into the endpoint unary capacities of $u$ and $v$ and placing a single undirected edge $u \leftrightarrow v$ of capacity $\frac{1}{2}(E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e)$!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation (`合并点边法` with $2\times$ Scaling)

For each grid edge $e = \{u, v\}$, the $2 \times 2$ reward table is $\Pi_e = \begin{pmatrix} E^{\text{sci}}_e & 0 \\ 0 & E^{\text{art}}_e \end{pmatrix}$. Subtracting from $E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e$ gives the submodular regret matrix:

$$E_e(x_u, x_v) = \begin{pmatrix} E^{\text{art}}_e & E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e \\ E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e & E^{\text{sci}}_e \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \Delta_e = E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e \ge 0.$$

To keep every capacity an exact integer without division by $2$, multiply the entire objective by **$2$**! Then for each edge $e = \{u, v\}$:

$$2\,E_e(x_u, x_v) = E^{\text{art}}_e\big((1 - x_u) + (1 - x_v)\big) + E^{\text{sci}}_e(x_u + x_v) + \big(E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e\big)\big(x_u(1 - x_v) + x_v(1 - x_u)\big).$$

Summing over all students $u \in V_{\text{grid}}$ and all grid edges $e \in E_{\text{grid}}$ yields:

$$2\Phi(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{u \in V_{\text{grid}}} \left[ \Big(2A_u + \sum_{e \ni u} E^{\text{art}}_e\Big)(1 - x_u) + \Big(2B_u + \sum_{e \ni u} E^{\text{sci}}_e\Big)x_u \right] + \sum_{e = \{u, v\} \in E_{\text{grid}}} \big(E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e\big)|x_u - x_v|.$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Graph Compilation)

- **Vertex Count**: Only $NM + 2 \le 10\,002$ vertices ($0$ auxiliary hubs, a **$5\times$ reduction** in vertex count compared to Method A!).
- **Scaled Accumulators**:
  - Initialize $p_u = 2 A_u$, $q_u = 2 B_u$ for each cell $u$, and `scaled_base` $= 2\sum_u (A_u + B_u)$.
  - For each grid edge $e = \{u, v\}$ with bonuses $(E^{\text{art}}_e, E^{\text{sci}}_e)$:
    - `scaled_base` $\mathrel{+}= 2(E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e)$.
    - $p_u \mathrel{+}= E^{\text{art}}_e, \; p_v \mathrel{+}= E^{\text{art}}_e$.
    - $q_u \mathrel{+}= E^{\text{sci}}_e, \; q_v \mathrel{+}= E^{\text{sci}}_e$.
    - Emit undirected grid edge **$u \xleftrightarrow{E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e} v$**.
  - Finally, apply Recipe 1 (`差値正規化`) to $(p_u, q_u)$ at each cell $u$, run Dinic, and output `(scaled_base - MaxFlow) / 2`!

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

Suppose a $1 \times 2$ grid has $A = (10, 0)$, $B = (0, 10)$, and edge $e = \{1, 2\}$ with $E^{\text{art}}_e = 5, E^{\text{sci}}_e = 7$.

- `scaled_base` $= 2(10 + 10) + 2(5 + 7) = 64$.
- Vertex $1$: $p_1 = 2(10) + 5 = 25$, $q_1 = 2(0) + 7 = 7 \implies m_1 = 7$, arc $S \xrightarrow{18} 1$.
- Vertex $2$: $p_2 = 2(0) + 5 = 5$, $q_2 = 2(10) + 7 = 27 \implies m_2 = 5$, arc $2 \xrightarrow{22} T$.
- Edge $1 \leftrightarrow 2$: capacity $5 + 7 = 12$.
- Minimum cut: $m_1 + m_2 + \min(18, 12, 22) = 7 + 5 + 12 = 24$.
- Maximum happiness: $(64 - 24) / 2 = 20$ (exact integer!).

> [!CAUTION]
> **Failure-Mode Guard (`Luogu P1646`)**: Notice that in our trace, $E^{\text{art}}_e = 5$ and $E^{\text{sci}}_e = 7$ are both **odd**! If you did not multiply capacities by $2$ and instead used integer division `5 / 2 = 2`, you would lose $1$ unit of capacity per odd edge and get WA. Always scale by $2\times$ before building the integer network and divide by $2$ at the very end!

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints (`#077` — Luogu P1646)"}
- **Hint 1**: Because every deskmate pair $\{u, v\}$ has size $2$, you can eliminate all $4NM$ auxiliary pair-hubs using Symmetric Half-Edge Compilation (`合并点边法`).
- **Hint 2**: Multiply all unary rewards $A_u, B_u$ by $2$. Then for each edge $e = \{u, v\}$, add $E^{\text{art}}_e$ to $p_u$ and $p_v$, add $E^{\text{sci}}_e$ to $q_u$ and $q_v$, and add an undirected edge $u \leftrightarrow v$ of capacity $E^{\text{art}}_e + E^{\text{sci}}_e$.
- **Hint 3**: Apply Recipe 1 (`差値正規化`) to $(p_u, q_u)$ at each cell, run Dinic, and divide the net scaled score by $2$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="C++ Model Compilation (`#077` — Luogu P1646: happiness via `合并点边法`)"}
```cpp
void solve_p1646() {
    int N, M;
    cin >> N >> M;
    int NM = N * M;
    auto id = [&](int r, int c) { return r * M + c + 1; };

    vector<long long> p(NM + 1, 0), q(NM + 1, 0);
    long long scaled_base = 0;

    // 1. Unary Arts rewards A_{r,c} (scaled by 2)
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) {
            long long a;
            cin >> a;
            p[id(r, c)] += 2 * a;
            scaled_base += 2 * a;
        }
    }
    // 2. Unary Science rewards B_{r,c} (scaled by 2)
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) {
            long long b;
            cin >> b;
            q[id(r, c)] += 2 * b;
            scaled_base += 2 * b;
        }
    }

    // Store undirected edge capacities between adjacent cells
    // Vertical pairs: (r, c) <-> (r+1, c) for r in [0, N-2], c in [0, M-1]
    // Horizontal pairs: (r, c) <-> (r, c+1) for r in [0, N-1], c in [0, M-2]
    vector<vector<long long>> cap_down(N - 1, vector<long long>(M, 0));
    vector<vector<long long>> cap_right(N, vector<long long>(M - 1, 0));

    // 3. Vertical Arts bonuses (N-1 rows, M cols)
    for (int r = 0; r < N - 1; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) {
            long long w;
            cin >> w;
            int u = id(r, c), v = id(r + 1, c);
            scaled_base += 2 * w;
            p[u] += w; p[v] += w;
            cap_down[r][c] += w;
        }
    }
    // 4. Vertical Science bonuses (N-1 rows, M cols)
    for (int r = 0; r < N - 1; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c) {
            long long w;
            cin >> w;
            int u = id(r, c), v = id(r + 1, c);
            scaled_base += 2 * w;
            q[u] += w; q[v] += w;
            cap_down[r][c] += w;
        }
    }
    // 5. Horizontal Arts bonuses (N rows, M-1 cols)
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M - 1; ++c) {
            long long w;
            cin >> w;
            int u = id(r, c), v = id(r, c + 1);
            scaled_base += 2 * w;
            p[u] += w; p[v] += w;
            cap_right[r][c] += w;
        }
    }
    // 6. Horizontal Science bonuses (N rows, M-1 cols)
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r) {
        for (int c = 0; c < M - 1; ++c) {
            long long w;
            cin >> w;
            int u = id(r, c), v = id(r, c + 1);
            scaled_base += 2 * w;
            q[u] += w; q[v] += w;
            cap_right[r][c] += w;
        }
    }

    int S = 0, T = NM + 1;
    Dinic<long long> G(T + 1);
    long long cut_offset = 0;

    for (int u = 1; u <= NM; ++u) {
        long long m = min(p[u], q[u]);
        cut_offset += m;
        if (p[u] > q[u]) G.add_edge(S, u, p[u] - q[u], 0);
        else if (q[u] > p[u]) G.add_edge(u, T, q[u] - p[u], 0);
    }
    for (int r = 0; r < N - 1; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < M; ++c)
            if (cap_down[r][c] > 0)
                G.add_edge(id(r, c), id(r + 1, c), cap_down[r][c], cap_down[r][c]);
    for (int r = 0; r < N; ++r)
        for (int c = 0; c < M - 1; ++c)
            if (cap_right[r][c] > 0)
                G.add_edge(id(r, c), id(r, c + 1), cap_right[r][c], cap_right[r][c]);

    long long min_cut = cut_offset + G.max_flow(S, T);
    cout << (scaled_base - min_cut) / 2 << "\n";
}
```

### `#078` (`Adv-2`) — Luogu P1791 / BZOJ 2039 [2009国家集训队]: 人员雇佣 (Employee Hiring)

- **Judge URL**: `https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P1791` / `https://darkbzoj.cc/problem/2039`
- **Constraints**: $N \le 1000$ candidates, hiring costs $A_i \le 10^9$, dense $N \times N$ synergy matrix $E_{i,j} \le 10^9$ ($E_{i,j} = E_{j,i}, E_{i,i} = 0$). Time Limit: 1.0 s.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)

Hiring candidate $i$ ($x_i = 1$) costs a salary $A_i \ge 0$. For every ordered pair $(i, j)$:

- If **both** $i$ and $j$ are hired ($x_i = x_j = 1$), the company gains $+E_{i,j}$ (so an unordered pair $\{i, j\}$ yields $+2 E_{i,j}$ when both are hired).
- If **$i$ is hired and $j$ is NOT hired** ($x_i = 1, x_j = 0$), the company suffers a friction penalty of **$-E_{i,j}$**!
- If $i$ is not hired ($x_i = 0$), $(i, j)$ contributes $0$.

Why is this an Advanced milestone? Because $N = 1000$ and the matrix $E_{i,j}$ is **completely dense** ($\binom{N}{2} \approx 5 \cdot 10^5$ pairs)! If you treat each pair $\{i, j\}$ as an auxiliary hub node (`Luogu P4174 最大获利` style), the network has $N + \binom{N}{2} \approx 5 \cdot 10^5$ vertices and $1.5 \cdot 10^6$ edges with huge capacities, which **TLEs and MLEs**. Instead, expanding the $2 \times 2$ matrix collapses the entire problem onto **$N + 2 = 1002$ vertices**!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation ($O(N)$ Vertex Degree-Collapse)

For each unordered pair $\{i, j\}$ ($1 \le i < j \le N$), combine the $(i, j)$ and $(j, i)$ contributions into a single $2 \times 2$ reward matrix $\Pi_{i,j}(x_i, x_j)$:

| $x_i \setminus x_j$ | $x_j = 0$ (Unhired) | $x_j = 1$ (Hired) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **$x_i = 0$ (Unhired)** | $0$ | $-E_{i,j}$ |
| **$x_i = 1$ (Hired)** | $-E_{i,j}$ | $+2 E_{i,j}$ |

Let us apply the **Asymmetric or Symmetric Cut Expansion** directly to $\Pi_{i,j}(x_i, x_j)$! Using the identity $2 x_i x_j = x_i + x_j - x_i(1 - x_j) - x_j(1 - x_i)$:

$$\begin{aligned}
\Pi_{i,j}(x_i, x_j) &= 2 E_{i,j} x_i x_j - E_{i,j} x_i(1 - x_j) - E_{i,j} x_j(1 - x_i) \\
&= E_{i,j}(x_i + x_j) - 2 E_{i,j}\big(x_i(1 - x_j) + x_j(1 - x_i)\big)!
\end{aligned}$$

Look at that miracle of cancellation:

1. Every fraction $\frac{1}{2}$ vanished completely—all coefficients are **exact integers**!
2. When we sum $E_{i,j}(x_i + x_j)$ over all unordered pairs $1 \le i < j \le N$, each candidate $i$ simply collects their **row sum** $D_i := \sum_{j=1}^N E_{i,j}$ as a unary profit $+D_i x_i$!
3. Each unordered pair $\{i, j\}$ simply becomes an **undirected edge $i \leftrightarrow j$ of capacity $2 E_{i,j}$**!

Therefore, the total net profit over all $\mathbf{x} \in \{0, 1\}^N$ is:

$$\Psi(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^N D_i - \left[ \sum_{i=1}^N D_i(1 - x_i) + \sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i + \sum_{1 \le i < j \le N} 2 E_{i,j}\big(x_i(1 - x_j) + x_j(1 - x_i)\big) \right].$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Graph Compilation)

- **Vertices**: $S = 0$, candidates $1 \dots N$, $T = N + 1$ ($1002$ vertices total!).
- **Baseline**: $W_{\text{base}} = \sum_{i=1}^N D_i = \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^N E_{i,j}$.
- **Unary Arcs (via Recipe 1)**: For each candidate $i$, apply Recipe 1 to $D_i(1 - x_i) + A_i x_i$:
  - Subtract $\min(D_i, A_i)$ from $W_{\text{base}}$.
  - If $D_i > A_i$, wire **$S \xrightarrow{D_i - A_i} i$**; if $A_i > D_i$, wire **$i \xrightarrow{A_i - D_i} T$**.
- **Pairwise Arcs**: For each $1 \le i < j \le N$, wire **$i \xleftrightarrow{2 E_{i,j}} j$** (`G.add_edge(i, j, 2 * E[i][j], 2 * E[i][j])`).

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

Suppose $N = 2$ with salaries $A = (5, 6)$ and synergy $E_{1,2} = E_{2,1} = 4$.

- Row sums: $D_1 = 4, D_2 = 4$; initial $W_{\text{base}} = 4 + 4 = 8$.
- Candidate $1$: $4(1 - x_1) + 5x_1 = 4 + 1x_1 \implies$ subtract $4$, arc $1 \xrightarrow{1} T$.
- Candidate $2$: $4(1 - x_2) + 6x_2 = 4 + 2x_2 \implies$ subtract $4$, arc $2 \xrightarrow{2} T$.
- Pairwise edge: $1 \xleftrightarrow{8} 2$.
- Remaining $W_{\text{base}} = 8 - 4 - 4 = 0$, and since $S$ has no outgoing edges, $\text{MaxFlow} = 0 \implies$ answer $0$ (hire neither; hiring both gives $8 - 5 - 6 = -3 < 0$). If instead $A = (2, 3)$, then $S \xrightarrow{2} 1$, $S \xrightarrow{1} 2$, $\text{MaxFlow} = 0$, and $W_{\text{base}} - \min = (8 - 2 - 3) - 0 = 3$ (hire both!).

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints (`#078` — Luogu P1791 / BZOJ 2039)"}
- **Hint 1**: Write the $2 \times 2$ payoff table for an unordered pair $\{i, j\}$: $(0,0) \mapsto 0$, $(1,0) \mapsto -E_{ij}$, $(0,1) \mapsto -E_{ij}$, $(1,1) \mapsto +2E_{ij}$.
- **Hint 2**: Verify that $E_{ij}(x_i + x_j) - 2E_{ij}\big(x_i(1 - x_j) + x_j(1 - x_i)\big)$ matches all four entries of that $2 \times 2$ table!
- **Hint 3**: Sum $E_{ij}(x_i + x_j)$ over all pairs so vertex $i$ gets unary reward $D_i = \sum_{j=1}^N E_{ij}$ against cost $A_i$, and each pair $\{i, j\}$ gets an undirected edge of capacity $2E_{ij}$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="C++ Model Compilation (`#078` — Luogu P1791 / BZOJ 2039: 人员雇佣)"}
```cpp
void solve_p1791() {
    int N;
    cin >> N;
    vector<long long> A(N + 1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) cin >> A[i];

    vector<vector<long long>> E(N + 1, vector<long long>(N + 1));
    vector<long long> D(N + 1, 0);
    long long ans_base = 0;

    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= N; ++j) {
            cin >> E[i][j];
            D[i] += E[i][j];
        }
        ans_base += D[i];
    }

    int S = 0, T = N + 1;
    Dinic<long long> G(T + 1);

    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) {
        long long m = min(D[i], A[i]);
        ans_base -= m;
        if (D[i] > A[i]) G.add_edge(S, i, D[i] - A[i], 0);
        else if (A[i] > D[i]) G.add_edge(i, T, A[i] - D[i], 0);
    }

    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) {
        for (int j = i + 1; j <= N; ++j) {
            long long cap = E[i][j] + E[j][i]; // 2 * E_{i,j}
            if (cap > 0) G.add_edge(i, j, cap, cap);
        }
    }

    cout << ans_base - G.max_flow(S, T) << "\n";
}
```

### `#079` (`Mas-1`) — Codeforces 311 E: Biologist

- **Judge URL**: `https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/311/E`
- **Constraints**: $N \le 10^4$ dogs, $M \le 2000$ experiments, friend anger penalty $g \le 10^4$; surgery costs $v_i \le 10^4$, experiment rewards $W_k \le 10^4$. Time Limit: 1.5 s.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)

Each dog $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ starts with binary state $s_i \in \{0, 1\}$, and flipping $x_i \neq s_i$ costs $v_i \ge 0$. Each of $M$ experiments specifies a target state $w_k \in \{0, 1\}$, a subset of dogs $C_k$, a reward $W_k \ge 0$ if $\forall i \in C_k, x_i = w_k$, and a boolean flag $f_k \in \{0, 1\}$: if the experiment **fails** ($\exists i \in C_k, x_i \neq w_k$) and $f_k = 1$, we not only lose $W_k$, we must **also pay a penalty $-g$ out of pocket**!

This problem tests whether you truly understand the algebraic difference between **Optimistic Baseline Pre-Claiming ($W_{\text{base}}$)** and **Regret Arc Capacity ($c_e$)**: when a friend's experiment fails, the net swing between success ($+W_k$) and failure ($-g$) is **$W_k - (-g) = W_k + g$**!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

Let $\sigma_k(\mathbf{x}) \in \{0, 1\}$ denote whether experiment $k$ succeeds ($\sigma_k = \prod_{i \in C_k} x_i$ if $w_k = 1$, or $\prod_{i \in C_k} (1 - x_i)$ if $w_k = 0$). The net payoff of experiment $k$ is:

$$W_k \sigma_k(\mathbf{x}) - g \cdot f_k \big(1 - \sigma_k(\mathbf{x})\big) = \underbrace{W_k}_{\text{add to } W_{\text{base}}} - \underbrace{(W_k + g \cdot f_k)}_{\text{hub arc capacity!}}\big(1 - \sigma_k(\mathbf{x})\big).$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Mechanical Graph Compilation)

- **Baseline**: $W_{\text{base}} = \sum_{k=1}^M W_k$ *(pre-claim ONLY $W_k$, NOT $W_k + g \cdot f_k$!)*.
- **Dog Unary Arcs**: If $s_i = 1$, wire **$S \xrightarrow{v_i} i$** (cost $v_i$ if flipped to $x_i = 0$); if $s_i = 0$, wire **$i \xrightarrow{v_i} T$** (cost $v_i$ if flipped to $x_i = 1$).
- **Experiment Hub Arcs ($h_k = N + k$)**: Let $C^{\text{regret}}_k = W_k + g \cdot f_k$.
  - If $w_k = 1$ (`All-in-S`): wire **$S \xrightarrow{C^{\text{regret}}_k} h_k$** and **$h_k \xrightarrow{\infty} i$** for all $i \in C_k$.
  - If $w_k = 0$ (`All-in-T`): wire **$i \xrightarrow{\infty} h_k$** for all $i \in C_k$ and **$h_k \xrightarrow{C^{\text{regret}}_k} T$**.

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

Suppose $N = 1$ dog with $s_1 = 0, v_1 = 10$, and $1$ friend experiment ($f_1 = 1, g = 5$) requiring $w_1 = 1$ on $C_1 = \{1\}$ with reward $W_1 = 3$.

- $W_{\text{base}} = 3$, and hub capacity is $W_1 + g = 3 + 5 = 8$.
- Path $S \xrightarrow{8} h_1 \xrightarrow{\infty} 1 \xrightarrow{10} T$ has bottleneck $\min(8, 10) = 8$.
- Net profit: $W_{\text{base}} - \text{MinCut} = 3 - 8 = -5$ (we leave $x_1 = 0$ to avoid paying $v_1 = 10$, failing the friend's experiment and paying $-g = -5$).

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints (`#079` — Codeforces 311E)"}
- **Hint 1**: Write the net contribution of experiment $k$ in both states: $+W_k$ when it succeeds, and $-g \cdot f_k$ when it fails.
- **Hint 2**: Rewrite that two-state payoff as $W_k - (W_k + g \cdot f_k)(1 - \sigma_k)$.
- **Hint 3**: Add only $W_k$ to `W_base`, while setting the hub's source/sink edge capacity to $W_k + g \cdot f_k$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="C++ Model Compilation (`#079` — Codeforces 311E: Biologist)"}
```cpp
void solve_cf311e() {
    int N, M;
    long long g;
    cin >> N >> M >> g;

    vector<int> s(N + 1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) cin >> s[i];

    int S = 0, T = N + M + 1;
    Dinic<long long> G(T + 1);
    const long long INF = 1e15;

    for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) {
        long long v;
        cin >> v;
        if (s[i] == 1) G.add_edge(S, i, v);
        else           G.add_edge(i, T, v);
    }

    long long W_base = 0;
    for (int k = 1; k <= M; ++k) {
        int w_k, K;
        long long W_k;
        cin >> w_k >> W_k >> K;
        W_base += W_k;
        vector<int> dogs(K);
        for (int j = 0; j < K; ++j) cin >> dogs[j];
        int is_friend;
        cin >> is_friend;

        long long regret_cap = W_k + (is_friend ? g : 0);
        int hub = N + k;
        if (w_k == 1) {
            G.add_edge(S, hub, regret_cap);
            for (int d : dogs) G.add_edge(hub, d, INF);
        } else {
            for (int d : dogs) G.add_edge(d, hub, INF);
            G.add_edge(hub, T, regret_cap);
        }
    }

    cout << W_base - G.max_flow(S, T) << "\n";
}
```

### `#080` (`Mas-2`) — Codeforces 1383 F: Special Edges

- **Judge URL**: `https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1383/F`
- **Constraints**: $N \le 10^4$ vertices, $M \le 10^4$ directed edges, $K \le 10$ special edges (the first $K$ edges), $Q \le 2 \cdot 10^5$ queries; all edge capacities $w_e \in [0, 25]$. Time Limit: 5.0 s.

#### Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal (Recognition)

We are given a directed network with $N, M \le 10^4$ where all capacities are tiny integers $\le 25$. In each of $Q = 2 \cdot 10^5$ independent queries, the capacities of the first $K \le 10$ **special edges** are updated to new values $(w_1, \dots, w_K) \in [0, 25]^K$, and we must report the $(1, N)$ maximum flow.

Running Dinic from scratch $Q = 2 \cdot 10^5$ times is $10^5\times$ too slow. The diagnostic clue is **$K \le 10$**: in any $(1, N)$-cut $(V_S, V_T)$, each of the $K$ special edges $e_r = (u_r \to v_r)$ is either **severed** ($\text{mask}_r = 1$) or **uncut** ($\text{mask}_r = 0$). There are only $2^K = 1024$ possible special-edge cut masks!

#### Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation ($2^K$ Parametric Cut Decomposition)

Separate the cut polynomial $\Phi_{\mathcal{N}}(\mathbf{x})$ into the $K$ special edges $E_{\text{spec}} = \{e_0, \dots, e_{K-1}\}$ and the $M - K$ static edges $E_{\text{static}}$:

$$\Phi_{\mathcal{N}}(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{w}) = \sum_{r=0}^{K-1} w_r\,x_{u_r}(1 - x_{v_r}) + \sum_{e \in E_{\text{static}}} c_e\,x_{u_e}(1 - x_{v_e}).$$

For any subset (bitmask) $\text{mask} \in \{0, \dots, 2^K - 1\}$ of special edges that are **NOT severed** (i.e., forced to remain uncut by giving them capacity $+\infty$, or bounded by $w_{\max} = 25$), define the **residual static cut table**:

$$F_{\text{static}}[\text{mask}] := \min_{\substack{\mathbf{x} \in \{0, 1\}^N \\ x_1 = 1, x_N = 0}} \left( \sum_{r \in \text{mask}} \infty \cdot x_{u_r}(1 - x_{v_r}) + \sum_{e \in E_{\text{static}}} c_e\,x_{u_e}(1 - x_{v_e}) \right).$$

Then by Max-Flow Min-Cut Duality, for **any** query weight vector $\mathbf{w} = (w_0, \dots, w_{K-1})$, the minimum $(1, N)$-cut is simply the minimum over all $2^K$ masks of (uncut mask's static cut $+$ sum of severed special edges outside `mask`):

$$\boxed{\text{MaxFlow}(\mathbf{w}) = \min_{\text{mask} \in \{0, \dots, 2^K - 1\}} \left( F_{\text{static}}[\text{mask}] + \sum_{r \notin \text{mask}} w_r \right)}$$

#### Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Incremental Residual Tree & Rollback)

How do we compute $F_{\text{static}}[\text{mask}]$ for all $2^K = 1024$ masks without running Dinic $1024$ times?

1. **Base Max-Flow ($\text{mask} = 0$)**: Set all $K$ special edges to capacity $0$ and run Dinic **once** to compute $F_{\text{static}}[0]$. Freeze this residual network!
2. **Incremental Single-Edge Augmentation ($w_{\max} = 25$)**: Since every query satisfies $w_r \le 25$, no special edge ever needs capacity larger than $25$ to act as $\infty$ relative to any valid query! When we transition from `mask` to `mask | (1 << r)` by setting special edge $e_r = (u_r \to v_r)$'s capacity from $0$ to $25$, the maximum flow increases by **at most $25$ units**!
3. **Recursion Tree with Residual Snapshots / Rollback**: Traverse the $2^K$ subsets via a recursive DFS over $r = 0 \dots K - 1$ (or in Gray-code order). Before branching into `mask | (1 << r)`, snapshot the current residual capacities (or record the modified edges on an undo stack), add $25$ to $e_r$'s forward capacity, and push at most $25$ augmenting units from $1$ to $N$ using simple BFS/DFS Ford–Fulkerson steps!
4. **$O(2^K)$ Query Evaluation**: For each query $(w_0, \dots, w_{K-1})$, compute the subset sums $W[\text{sub}] = \sum_{r \in \text{sub}} w_r$ in $O(2^K)$ time via `W[m] = W[m ^ lsb] + w[ctz(m)]`, and take $\min_{\text{mask}} \big(F_{\text{static}}[\text{mask}] + W[(2^K - 1) \oplus \text{mask}]\big)$ in $1024$ integer operations!

#### Step 4: Hand-Checkable Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard

Suppose $N = 2$ ($S = 1, T = 2$) with $1$ static edge $1 \xrightarrow{10} 2$ and $K = 1$ special edge $e_0 = (1 \to 2)$.

- $\text{mask} = 0$ ($e_0$ has cap $0$): $F_{\text{static}}[0] = 10$.
- $\text{mask} = 1$ ($e_0$ has cap $25$): $F_{\text{static}}[1] = 10 + 25 = 35$.
- For a query with $w_0 = 7$: $\min\big(F_{\text{static}}[0] + w_0, \; F_{\text{static}}[1] + 0\big) = \min(10 + 7, 35) = 17$.

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="3-Tier Progressive Hints (`#080` — Codeforces 1383F)"}
- **Hint 1**: Any $(1, N)$-cut partitions the $K \le 10$ special edges into a severed subset ($\overline{\text{mask}}$) and an uncut subset ($\text{mask}$).
- **Hint 2**: Since $w_r \le 25$, giving each uncut special edge $r \in \text{mask}$ capacity $25$ is equivalent to giving it capacity $+\infty$.
- **Hint 3**: Compute $F_{\text{static}}[0]$ with Dinic, then use a depth-$K$ recursion tree that snapshots residual capacities and augments edge $e_r$ (capacity $25$) using simple Ford–Fulkerson DFS/BFS paths!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="C++ Model Compilation (`#080` — Codeforces 1383F: Special Edges)"}
```cpp
// Compact residual network supporting O(M) snapshot copy for the K <= 10 recursion tree
struct IncrementalFlow {
    struct Edge { int to, rev, cap; };
    int N;
    vector<vector<Edge>> adj;
    vector<int> spec_u, spec_idx;

    IncrementalFlow(int n) : N(n), adj(n + 1) {}

    int add_edge(int u, int v, int cap) {
        int idx = adj[u].size();
        adj[u].push_back({v, (int)adj[v].size(), cap});
        adj[v].push_back({u, idx, 0});
        return idx;
    }

    // Standard single-path DFS/BFS augmentation for small <= 25 increments
    int augment_up_to_25(int S, int T) {
        int pushed_total = 0;
        vector<int> par_v(N + 1), par_e(N + 1), q(N + 1);
        while (true) {
            fill(par_v.begin(), par_v.end(), -1);
            int qh = 0, qt = 0;
            q[qt++] = S;
            par_v[S] = S;
            int found_bot = 0;
            while (qh < qt) {
                int u = q[qh++];
                if (u == T) break;
                for (int i = 0; i < (int)adj[u].size(); ++i) {
                    const auto& e = adj[u][i];
                    if (e.cap > 0 && par_v[e.to] == -1) {
                        par_v[e.to] = u;
                        par_e[e.to] = i;
                        q[qt++] = e.to;
                        if (e.to == T) break;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (par_v[T] == -1) break;
            int bot = 25;
            for (int v = T; v != S; v = par_v[v])
                bot = min(bot, adj[par_v[v]][par_e[v]].cap);
            for (int v = T; v != S; v = par_v[v]) {
                int u = par_v[v], ei = par_e[v];
                int rev = adj[u][ei].rev;
                adj[u][ei].cap -= bot;
                adj[v][rev].cap += bot;
            }
            pushed_total += bot;
        }
        return pushed_total;
    }
};

void solve_cf1383f() {
    int N, M, K, Q;
    cin >> N >> M >> K >> Q;
    IncrementalFlow G(N);
    vector<int> spec_u(K), spec_e(K);

    for (int i = 0; i < M; ++i) {
        int u, v, w;
        cin >> u >> v >> w;
        if (i < K) {
            spec_u[i] = u;
            spec_e[i] = G.add_edge(u, v, 0); // Initially 0 in base network
        } else {
            G.add_edge(u, v, w);
        }
    }

    // 1. Base max-flow on static edges (use Dinic on G in production)
    int base_flow = 0;
    while (int df = G.augment_up_to_25(1, N)) base_flow += df;

    // 2. Precompute F_static[mask] for all 2^K masks via recursion tree with snapshots
    vector<int> F_static(1 << K, 0);
    auto dfs = [&](auto& self, int bit, int mask, int cur_flow) -> void {
        if (bit == K) {
            F_static[mask] = cur_flow;
            return;
        }
        // Branch 0: special edge `bit` stays at capacity 0 (severed if used)
        self(self, bit + 1, mask, cur_flow);

        // Snapshot current residual capacities before adding capacity 25 to edge `bit`
        auto saved_adj = G.adj;
        G.adj[spec_u[bit]][spec_e[bit]].cap += 25;
        int add_flow = G.augment_up_to_25(1, N);
        self(self, bit + 1, mask | (1 << bit), cur_flow + add_flow);
        G.adj = move(saved_adj); // Rollback residual graph
    };
    dfs(dfs, 0, 0, base_flow);

    // 3. Answer Q queries in O(2^K) per query
    int full_mask = (1 << K) - 1;
    vector<int> W_sub(1 << K, 0), w(K);
    while (Q--) {
        for (int i = 0; i < K; ++i) cin >> w[i];
        for (int m = 1; m < (1 << K); ++m) {
            int b = __builtin_ctz(m);
            W_sub[m] = W_sub[m ^ (1 << b)] + w[b];
        }
        int ans = 1e9;
        for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << K); ++mask) {
            ans = min(ans, F_static[mask] + W_sub[full_mask ^ mask]);
        }
        cout << ans << "\n";
    }
}
```

## 7. Pre-Submission Checklist (`FM-10` Audit)

Before submitting any Pseudo-Boolean Cut / Burn-or-Bury solution, run through this 6-point verification checklist:

1. **Explicit Binary Dictionary ($S$ vs. $T$)**: Did you write down at the top of your scratchpad whether $x_i = 1$ means $i \in V_S$ ($S \to i$ severed when $x_i = 0$) or $i \in V_T$? Never mix conventions mid-problem!
2. **Kolmogorov–Zabih Submodularity Check ($A + D \le B + C$)**: For every pairwise penalty table $E_{u,v}$, did you verify $\Delta_{uv} = (B + C) - (A + D) \ge 0$? If $\Delta_{uv} < 0$, did you check for a bipartite variable flip (Chapter 11)?
3. **Asymmetric vs. Symmetric $2\times$ Scaling**: If you used Symmetric Half-Edge Compilation (`合并点边法`, `#077`), did you multiply all unary and pairwise capacities by **$2$** so that odd $\Delta_{uv}$ values do not truncate under integer division?
4. **Separate All-$S$ and All-$T$ Synergy Hubs (`FM-10` Bug 4)**: When a subset $C$ has both an All-$S$ bonus ($y_C$) and an All-$T$ bonus ($z_C$), did you allocate **two distinct vertex IDs** $y_C \neq z_C$?
5. **Hub Implication Direction & Self-Inclusion (`FM-10` Bug 3 & `#076`)**: Does flow travel strictly from $S \xrightarrow{B_C} y_C \xrightarrow{\infty} i \xrightarrow{\infty} z_C \xrightarrow{B'_C} T$? And on grid stencils (`文理分科`), did your direction loop include `(dr = 0, dc = 0)` so the center cell is connected to its own hub?
6. **Optimistic Baseline vs. Regret Swing (`#079` `CF 311E`)**: When failing a clause incurs an extra out-of-pocket penalty $-g$ in addition to losing reward $+W_k$, did you add **only $W_k$** to `W_base` while setting the hub's cut capacity to **$W_k + g$**?

## 8. Chapter Summary & Bridge to Chapter 11

In this chapter, we unified binary minimum-cut modelling under the algebraic language of **Pseudo-Boolean Cut Polynomials**:

- Every $(S, T)$-cut network with non-negative capacities evaluates a polynomial $\Phi_{\mathcal{N}}(\mathbf{x}) = C_0 + \sum_u c_{S \to u}(1 - x_u) + \sum_u c_{u \to T} x_u + \sum_{u \neq v} c_{u \to v} x_u(1 - x_v)$.
- By the **Kolmogorov–Zabih Submodularity Theorem (Theorem 10.1)**, a $2 \times 2$ penalty matrix $\begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ C & D \end{pmatrix}$ is graph-representable with non-negative capacities if and only if **$A + D \le B + C$** ($\Delta_{uv} = B + C - A - D \ge 0$). When submodular, it compiles without auxiliary vertices via either the **Asymmetric Integer Split** ($\alpha = \Delta_{uv}, \beta = 0$) or **Hu Botao's Symmetric Half-Edge Split (`合并点边法`, $\alpha = \beta = \frac{1}{2}\Delta_{uv}$)**.
- Higher-order degree-$k$ unanimity bonuses $+B_C \prod_{i \in C} x_i$ and $+B'_C \prod_{i \in C} (1 - x_i)$ compile cleanly via **Theorem 10.2's Auxiliary Synergy Hubs ($y_C$ and $z_C$)**.
- For general non-submodular quadratic functions, **Roof Duality / QPBO (Theorem 10.3)** doubles the graph into $\{x_i, \bar{x}_i\}$, computing a half-integral LP optimum $\hat{\mathbf{x}} \in \{0, \frac{1}{2}, 1\}^N$ whose integral coordinates are **globally persistent**.

### Bridge to Chapter 11: What If $A + D > B + C$?

In Theorem 10.3(3), we glimpsed a tantalizing phenomenon: whenever the supermodular edges ($A + D > B + C$) form a **bipartite graph** $G = (L \sqcup R, E)$, the doubled QPBO network $\mathcal{N}_{\text{QPBO}}$ splits into two identical, disconnected halves—meaning the problem can be solved **100% integrally on $N$ vertices** by simply **inverting the binary variables $y_v := 1 - x_v$ on all right-side vertices $v \in R$**!

In **Chapter 11 (Pairwise Submodularity, Symmetric Penalties & Bipartite Variable Inversion `反転`)**, we turn this observation into one of the most powerful weapons in modern competitive programming: rescuing supermodular "zebra disagreement" bonuses (`ABC 193F`), row-column inclusion-exclusion conflicts (`ABC 259G`), and two-permutation cycle collisions (`AGC 038F — Two Permutations`).
